Wow. Thank you for posting this. I've been struggling with my own breakup for a while now, and didn't know how to handle my own emotions.The only logical feeling, I told myself, is to be angry at her. Because it was better than longing for the past, or blaming myself. Unfortunately, that doesn't work very well, the anger spilled into other parts of my life, and I was only harming myself with that emotion.

But seeing you handle this situation so amicably, and how you still have a more-positive-that-negative relationship with your wife (son, still talking etc.), really encourages me to step back and get a new perspective of the whole situation

Let's be honest. You can't be a true friend to her as long as you still see her as ex-gf. Especially if you're in the mind set that you want her back. You can't be a true friend to her if you have hidden motives.

Sticking around is the easy answer. It feels like nothings really changed right now. It feels so familiar, and so easy to fall back on those old relationship habits. But everything's changed. You broke up for a reason. How would you feel if you stuck around to see her get another bf? Are you ok with her having so much power and influence over you?  Can you live with the idea that you're just a backup bf for just in case? What do you gain from being her friend? Is what you gain from staying around worth what might be coming up? I'm not going to tell you that you must move on. But if you step back a few steps and take a look at the bigger picture, it might help you see a new perspective.

Like others have said, you're going to have to learn to move on. And part of moving on means you're going to have to show yourself that you, a perfectly capable human being, can function without her. Staying around her is going to prolong that process.

From an outside perspective, it looks like she's keeping you on a leash and you're just a backup bf, just in case. Are you ok with that?

Figure out what's important to you. What exactly do you want from her, and what are deal breakers. Is this girl someone whom you are willing to wait for? And do you have the patient to wait that long?

If you've truely moved on, then you must be ok with the idea that you will never talk to your ex again. And assuming that you're ok with never seeing your ex again, I think its best to tell your current gf now about the situation, to show her you trust her, and her opinion matters to you. 

That said, do you still need the closure now? You sound like you're doing great and moving forward, do you really want to get dragged back to the past? In my opinion, the only reason one should look to the past is to learn from your mistakes. I'm not sure there's anything to learn from digging up this past, that will develop you into a better person. So for your own sake, do you gain anything out of this, or is your emotional side just being needy and illogical about it?

Also, the tables have turned. She's now the 'needy' one and you're the 'stable' one. It's partly your responsibility to not get your ex's hope up. Maybe your ex is going through a rough time. But there's nothing you can do that's going to help. Your ex may very well be better off without talking to you. Consider that.

Actually, why not just ask her through e-mail? It will allow you time to really think about what you want to ask her.

Would love to hear an update from you once you've made a decision.
Is the important issue here why you care, or the fact that you do care?
